nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The great hearth of the Guild Hall of Steady Steps has been lit for longer than anyone can remember. This morning it is the colour of a very tired peach.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I have counted the logs. We have burned a winter's worth since midnight, and the fire is smaller than when we started. I would like it written down that I said so.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Nonsense! The answer to a low fire is a bigger fire! More logs! More bellows! I have not slept, and I have never felt more awake!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Chad, you've been standing there since the lamps went out. You're swaying a little.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: That is the sway of a man in command of a hearth!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Biscuit has left his place on the rug, which has gone cold, and moved to a stool beside the kettle. He is looking at the hearth the way you look at a friend who has stopped answering.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have been reading the old guild book, and there is a note in the margin. 'Do not feed the fire. Keep it.' It is underlined twice, and then somebody has drawn a very small cake.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: That is the founder's handwriting. It is the only note she ever wrote that I do not understand.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Keep it! I am keeping it! I am keeping it so hard!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Maybe keeping and feeding aren't the same thing?

options.label: Sit Chad down with a cup of tea.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Thank you. I have been trying to do that since three o'clock this morning.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: I am not sitting. I am leaning. Next to a chair. Companionably.

options.label: Help Maple read the old book.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: A second pair of eyes! I will make you a list. It will have only four things on it, which for me is a holiday.

options.label: Ask the fire what it wants.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Oh, I do like that. Nobody has asked it. We have all been telling it.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: The hearth gives one soft crackle, in the manner of a very old person clearing their throat.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The next page has a drawing of the door under the stairs, and beneath it, three words. 'Ask the smith.'

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: We have a smith?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: We have a door. I have always assumed it was a cupboard.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Item one hundred and five. Find out what is in the cupboard. Item one hundred and six: tea.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Right! Down we go! At speed! ...Maple?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: At your own pace, Chad. Nothing here has a deadline except the tea, which is cooling.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The cupboard under the stairs is not a cupboard. It is a landing, and past the landing is a stair, and the stair goes down in the confident manner of something that has been going down for years.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Forty-one steps, forty-two... I've lost count. I think that means we're very far down.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I count in sevens. It is far more restful, and nobody ever argues with a seven.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It is getting warmer with every step. The air smells like toast and old iron, in about equal parts.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Onward! Downward! At the speed of a legend! ...I am going to sit on this step for a moment. On purpose. Tactically.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You have been tactically sitting on every third step for the last ten minutes.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A hero must be well rested to meet a smith. Rest is training. I said that. Mostly. In a quieter voice.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: That's what I do too. Landing, breath, landing. It is the same stair, it just stops being long.

options.label: Carrying the lantern, so everyone can see.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: A lantern bearer! I shall write it down. The lantern bearer is the most important person on the stair, and also the one who gets to look at everyone's shoes.

options.label: Right behind Chad, just in case.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: That is the best seat on a staircase. I have held it for eleven years.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Something comes up the stair towards them, very fast, then stops, and sits down heavily on a step with its satchel in its lap. It has a red scarf.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Hello! I am fine! I have fallen over on the way up and I am being very calm about it.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Fennel! What are you doing under the hall?

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: Delivering. I come down this stair every spring and nobody has ever once said hello. It's been the loneliest post round in the valley, and it's mine.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I am so sorry. I assumed you were something from the cellar.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: I was something from the cellar! I've been something from the cellar for years!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Fennel digs in the satchel and produces a very old, very warm envelope. It says: FOR WHOEVER FINALLY ASKED.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: 'Dear whoever finally asked. The kettle has been on for eleven years. Bring a friend, bring a coat and do not, under any circumstances, bring more logs. Yours, B.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Do not bring more logs.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I have a great many logs. I had a great many. I used them all. I am going to put the remaining logs down now, gently, as if they were sleeping.

nodes.speaker: fennel
nodes.text: He means it kindly. He signs everything B. He has never once been late with a reply, and I have never once been on time with the post. It balances.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Come on. It's only a bit further. I can see a glow.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The stair ends in a room so warm and so orange that it feels like walking into the inside of a loaf. There is an anvil, a wall of tools, a furnace like an open mouth, and a very large person in an apron, who turns around slowly and takes his goggles off.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: Somebody knocked. In eleven years, that is the first knock that was not a goat.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Greetings! I am Chad, the guildmaster! I am here about the hearth, and I have brought everyone, and I have very nearly stopped bringing logs!

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: Brun. Forgemaster. I made your bell, your front door, your spoons, and, if I am honest, most of the swords in your cellar, about which I have opinions.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The cellar swords are very good swords.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: They are adequate. The third one on the left is a crime. I did it on a Tuesday.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Item one hundred and seven. Ask about the swords. Item one hundred and eight: do not ask about the swords.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: I have been waiting for someone to ask me which fire you want. A forge or a hearth. They are not the same fire.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A fire is a fire! Bigger is better! Hotter is more!

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: A forge burns hot for an hour and then it rests. A hearth burns low for a hundred years and never once stops. Different fire. Different fuel. The very same flame.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: I lit your hearth, a long time ago, from this forge. A very kind woman asked me to. Then she banked it, and left a note, and forgot to tell anyone how.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The founder. She forgot to tell anyone how.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: She was busy, and she trusted the fire. That is a thing you can only do once you have learned how to keep one.

nodes.prompt: What would you make, if Brun lent you the anvil?

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: A spoon! The best answer anyone has given me since a sword. Spoons are what hold the day together.

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: Small bells are a delight. They only ever say one thing, and they say it kindly.

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: Oh, no. I made one of those once. It argued with the cat for a decade. I will not do it again. I would do it again.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Can you show us how? The keeping? I think we'd all like to learn it properly.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: Gladly. But first you must meet whoever is sleeping under the coals, because it is her fire as much as it is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Beyond the forge the floor slopes into a cavern with a slow river of orange running through it. In the middle of the river, which should be impossible, there is a small, calm mountain with a face.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: That is Magmara, the Slow Simmer. The fire in your hearth is the end of her front step. She has been very kind about it.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: How do you do, Magmara! I am Bertram. I am eighty-four now, so I am rather good at waiting.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The mountain's eyes open, very slowly, in the way a window opens when the wind is thinking about it.

nodes.speaker: magmara
nodes.text: ...Hello.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: It takes her a little while. I always wait for the next word before I say anything.

nodes.prompt: How do you speak to Magmara?

reply.speaker: magmara
reply.text: ...Oh. Thank you. Most people talk as if the sentence were on fire. It is... a relief.

reply.speaker: magmara
reply.text: ...That was lovely. You asked, and then you left room. Hardly anyone leaves room.

reply.speaker: magmara
reply.text: ...Mm. I know that one. Someone hummed it above my head, for ten winters, while they were poking.

nodes.speaker: magmara
nodes.text: ...I am not annoyed. I want that understood. I have been not annoyed since the third winter. It is going very well.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Oh. Oh no. It's the logs, isn't it.

nodes.speaker: magmara
nodes.text: ...It is every night, for eleven years. A poke, and a poke, and a poke. They are very small pokes. I have a large front step.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...I may have been the poker.

nodes.speaker: magmara
nodes.text: ...You have a great deal of energy.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I do! I have! And I used all of it on the wrong end! I thought a fire was a thing you give your strength to, and it is a thing you give your patience to, and I have never once given my patience to anything!

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: He is learning. Look at his face. It is the face of a man who has put down a log.

nodes.speaker: magmara
nodes.text: ...Rest is training. Ask any mountain. You do not get to be a mountain by hurrying.

nodes.speaker: magmara
nodes.text: ...Poke less, banked more. I will keep the seam warm, if you keep the fire low. At my own pace. Nothing here has a deadline.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I accept! I accept all of it, very quietly!

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Item one hundred and nine. Learn how to leave room. I have a feeling it will fill the notebook.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: Banking a fire has four steps. Rake the coals to the middle. Cover them with ash. Leave a thumb of air. And walk away. The last one is the hardest.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Walk away! From a fire! That is the opposite of everything I believe in!

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: A fire that is watched every minute is a fire that is being fed every minute. Sooner or later it gets tired of the attention. You can trust it to know how.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Brun hands out rakes. Maple's is the right size. Bertram's is slightly too tall, so he holds it like a walking stick and pretends that is on purpose.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Rake to the middle. I can do a middle. I have been doing a middle for eleven years.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: The coals look so small, all piled up in the middle. Is that all the fire there is?

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: That is all the fire there ever is. The rest is show. A low red glow can keep a house warm for a week.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Chad takes his turn, with ash, with great seriousness. He covers the coals so thoroughly that for a moment the fire is gone entirely, and everyone holds their breath.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: That is too much cover. Smothering is not keeping. Lift a little. There. See it breathe?

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: It is breathing! I did that! Very well, with help! Mostly with help!

nodes.prompt: How much air does a banked fire need?

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: Exactly a thumb. Not a fist, not a finger. Yours is a very good thumb.

options.label: As much as it asks for.

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: That is the answer of someone who listens. It asks for very little, and very quietly, and a good keeper hears it.

options.label: Enough to breathe, and no more.

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: Enough to breathe, and no more. I will carve that over the door.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: People are the same, you know. A fire that blazes all night is out by morning. A fire that is kept is still there on Tuesday.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I think that was the founder's whole note. 'Do not feed the fire. Keep it.' She was not talking about logs.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I started at Level 2. I would like to try the rest of it at Level Banked.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: That's a very good level.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: Now take a coal home. Not a log, a coal. A small one, in a clay pot, with the lid on, carried carefully. It will light the hearth, and the hearth will do the rest.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The clay pot is not large. It is warm to hold, as heavy as a loaf, and the stair back up to the hall is four hundred and twelve steps and a few extra for luck.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: You do not carry a coal up a stair by yourself. That is how a coal goes out and a person goes red. You pass it. Hand to hand.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Word has gone up the stair, and down it, and round it. Footsteps are arriving: a yeti with a pot of soup, a lighthouse keeper in a yellow coat, and a Weatherkeeper who has come down her own steps and now, kindly, agrees to go up someone else's.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I brought soup. Nobody asked, which is the best time to bring it.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I brought a lantern, in case the stair is dark. It never quite goes out. Neither does Chad, but he is better in daylight.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: I came down by landings, and I will go up by landings. A step is a step. Everyone gets their turn at one.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: {hero}, you were going to give the guild a story, a song or an afternoon, if I remember. This is an afternoon.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: {hero} said they would give the guild a story. A stair is a very good length for one.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: {hero} said they would give a song. We have four hundred steps, and a song is about fifty steps long. We will need eight.

options.label: The steepest bit, in short turns.

reply.speaker: brun
reply.text: The steepest bit, where the pot wants to roll. A good place for someone who steps carefully.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: I shall be right behind you, saying nothing, extremely quietly!

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: The middle is where it gets long, and the story is what makes it short. Good choice.

options.label: The top, to hand it over.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: The last landing. Everyone dreams of it, and hardly anyone knows what to say when they arrive. You will.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The pot goes up. Hush to Wren, Wren to Tamsin, Tamsin to Chad, Chad, for the first time in his life, to somebody else without trying to carry it further. Each hand is warm for a minute, and then empty, and that is how it works.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I gave it away! I gave it away and it is still going! That is the most magnificent thing I have ever not done!

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: That is the whole of banking. You do not hold the fire. You hand it on.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: There is soup at the top. There is always soup at the top.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The hall is dark and the hearth is cold, and in the middle of the cold hearth, in a clay pot with its lid on, is a small red glow. Everyone has pulled up a chair and a blanket and is looking at it, politely.

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: Woof.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Biscuit says that the pot is the best thing that has ever happened, and I agree with him, and so does he.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Tomorrow we put it in the hearth, don't we? I don't want to do it tonight. It feels like it should wait for the morning.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Nothing here has a deadline. A fire is lit when it is ready, and not before. I think the founder would have liked that.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I would like to say something. I have written it down, so that I do not lose it. 'I came to this hall to begin. I have found that beginning is something you do over and over.' Item one hundred and ten.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I would also like to say something. I have a confession.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Chad.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I did not light the first fire. I have always said that I did. In fact I took a great deal of credit, and I stood very near it.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I lit it, the week you arrived. It was a wet Thursday, and you were out buying a bell. I let you say it was you.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: You let me?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You looked so pleased. I thought, a hall needs one person who stands near the fire and says it is theirs, and one who quietly knows how it works.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I am not even annoyed. That is the strangest part. I am just... deeply impressed.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I think that's the nicest thing anyone's ever said at a hearth.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Something small and bright is in {hero}'s hand: a little iron poker, no longer than a fork, with a tiny flame stamped on the handle. It was in the pot, tucked under the lid. A note is tied to it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: 'For the one who carried it. Do not poke. Keep it, and one day give it to someone who is just starting. Yours, B.'

nodes.prompt: What do you do with Brun's little poker?

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: By the hearth, where everyone passes it. I will put a hook up in the morning. I will measure it twice.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: A pocket is the finest place for a small useful thing. I have a poker, a pencil and a biscuit in mine.

options.label: Save it for someone who is just starting.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: I think that's exactly what it's for. Somebody gave me a mug once, a long time ago, and it is still my favourite thing.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Everybody sleep. The fire is in its pot, and the pot is in the hall, and the hall is, for once, not on fire or about to be.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: In the morning, light comes through the windows in the careful way it does when it has been invited. Brun has come up from below with soot on his goggles and an expression of high professional anxiety.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: I have not been in a hall for eleven years. I do not know where to put my hands. May I hold something?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Hold the kettle. It is a very forgiving kettle.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Maple rakes the cold ash to the sides. Pip lifts the lid of the pot. The coal inside is no bigger than a walnut, and it glows the way a sleeper breathes.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: The fire is the size of a walnut. I have been feeding fires the size of a cart, and I have never been so proud of anything.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Rake. Cover. A thumb of air. Walk away. I have it on a card.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Everyone takes a turn. Maple lays a little kindling, a handful of dry sticks, and no more. Pip tips the coal in. Bertram breathes a thumb's worth of air across it. Chad covers it with ash, carefully, and stops before it is too much.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: For a moment nothing happens. Then, in the dark of the grate, a small orange line appears, steady and low, like a pencil mark on a page.

nodes.speaker: brun
nodes.text: That is it. That is a hearth. It will be here at dawn, and next dawn, and the dawn after that, if you let it be.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: And now I walk away. Slowly. Do not look at me. I am walking away from a fire and it is the bravest thing I have done.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You will be back in four minutes to check it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Five. I am working on five.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: That evening, in the long gold hush after the last of the bowls have been put away, somebody knocks at the front door.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It is a person with a very small bag and a very large expression of not knowing where to begin. They are standing in the doorway, with the dark behind them and the firelight in front.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Good evening! Is this the place one begins? That is what I asked, when I was eighty-three. I was told it was.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It is. Come in. Mind the Duck Mat, everyone starts on the Duck Mat. I'll show you.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: There is soup, a chair and a kettle. In that order, or any order.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: A warm cup. It is a very small thing, and I would trade a great many large ones for it.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: Oh! That is the one meant for the one just starting. It has a little flame on the handle. Do not poke the hearth with it, and everything will be fine.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: A chair by the fire. It is always one of the best things you can offer, and it is free.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The newcomer sits. The hearth glows low and red and steady, as it has always meant to, and nobody leans in to feed it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Welcome to the Guild Hall of Steady Steps. Do not worry about a thing. I started at Level 1, like everyone.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Move however you like, rest when you need to, and always leave a thumb of air. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Have fun with it, the way you said you would, and bring somebody who is just starting. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Stay curious, the way you did from the very first day. There is always a new thing to keep. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Far away a bell rings, a lamp winks, a chime sings and a table is laid. Under all of it, in a hall on a hill, a small red fire is kept, at its own pace, with a thumb of air, and one chair by the hearth for whoever comes next.
